lines.say: Why does this happen, number twelve.
Everyone blames salt and water. But the evidence for that is weaker than you think.
The leading idea now: when a muscle gets very tired, the signals that switch it on get louder, and the signals that switch it off get weaker.
So the muscle gets stuck on.
Here's the weird proof. In one study, a sip of pickle juice stopped cramps in about eighty five seconds. Faster than water.
That's too fast to be the salt reaching your muscle. It's probably a reflex from the taste.
The fix right now: gently stretch the cramping muscle. That turns the off signal back on.
Next: why soreness hits two days later.
